prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general and mechanistically understood method for constructing aryl amines

statement.case_for: I keep palladium-catalysed C-N coupling as my preferred configuration after reading the full first round. It is the one shortlisted achievement that is mature, independently reproduced for three decades, mechanistically explained and attributable to two people without argument. The distinctness question raised by Linke and Sparr is the crux, and my answer is that the 2010 prize rewarded C-C coupling between carbon nucleophiles and electrophiles, whereas C-N coupling required solving different elementary-step problems: amine binding and deprotonation at palladium, competing beta-hydride elimination from amido complexes, and a slow C-N reductive elimination that only bulky, electron-rich ligands made facile. Buchwald and Hartwig each designed ligand families from mechanistic studies, and that design principle is what converted a niche tin-amide reaction into a method that is routine in pharmaceutical process chemistry, materials and total synthesis. A prize here would honour how chemists learned to make a bond they previously could not make reliably, which is the core test I apply as the committee's synthetic chemist.
statement.case_against: The honest weakness is perception and generative novelty. Many will read C-N coupling as a continuation of the 2010 paradigm, and the committee has no obligation to reward a refinement of recognised chemistry when a new modality such as targeted protein degradation is available. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide coupling is a genuine antecedent that a two-name prize cannot fully honour; I would accept acknowledgement in the background text, not a third laureate, because the general catalytic method is what the two laureates created. Finally, I have to admit that after round 1 my configuration still has one explicit supporter, and an easy attribution is not by itself a stronger scientific case, as Sparr rightly says.

responses.point: Linke asks whether the ligand-design principle behind C-N coupling is a distinct achievement or a refinement of the 2010 prize, and says he is not yet convinced it is distinct, which is why he ranks it below degradation.
responses.response: I think the test should be whether the problem was different, not whether the metal was the same. The 2010 prize solved how to join carbon fragments through transmetalation; amination needed amido-palladium chemistry in which beta-hydride elimination and sluggish C-N reductive elimination had to be suppressed by ligand design, and that took a separate research programme in two laboratories. I agree that this makes it a less dramatic story than degraders. I do not agree it makes it a refinement, and I would not hold the 2010 prize against it any more than the committee held the 2001 oxidation and hydrogenation prizes against each other. If the committee still prefers B027, I can live with that as my second choice, which I explain below.

responses.point: Chabes proposes B027 as a second part with Crews and Handa but not Deshaies, accepting that dropping Deshaies is a real cost with no clean solution.
responses.response: The cost is larger than your statement allows. Crews and Deshaies jointly conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC principle, and without that concept the cereblon mechanism would explain a drug but not create a modality. If degradation is recognised at all, the attribution that I find defensible is Crews, Deshaies and Handa as Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke name it. A Crews and Handa pair looks like an attempt to leave room under the three-person cap for Liu, and I would not shape a degradation citation around that. I also would not pair B038 with it, since the 2020 CRISPR prize makes base editing the weaker half.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that targeted protein degradation is a simple chemical idea that opened a new class of drug mechanism, covers both PROTAC and glue branches with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and passes his game-changer test.
responses.response: I accept the chemical clarity and the independent reproduction, and Handa's cereblon work does give the glue branch a mechanistic anchor that my earlier Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio lacked. Where I still differ is maturity. No degrader is approved as far as I know, so we would be honouring a promising modality before the medicine proves it. That is a timing judgement, not a scientific objection, and it is the main reason I keep B027 as an alternative rather than my choice. If members can say from the record that the chemistry is validated as a tool in laboratories worldwide, I would regard that as sufficient and would support your configuration over lipid nanoparticles or perovskites.

responses.point: Sparr says ionizable lipid nanoparticles are physical chemistry of self-assembled matter, that the 2023 Medicine overlap concerns the mRNA cargo, and that an easy attribution should not be treated as a stronger scientific case.
responses.response: Your last point is fair and I have restated my case on distinctness, not on convenience. On B062 I still cannot write a three-name citation I would defend: your trio of Cullis, Madden and Hope, Aili's earlier trio and the later work of MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each honour a different discovery, and as a synthetic chemist I cannot judge which of the structure-activity rules for ionizable lipids is a design principle and which is empirical screening. Your phase-behaviour argument is the strongest case for it being chemistry, but until the citation can state the principle in one sentence and the credited names follow from it, I would not rank it above a method whose credit is not in dispute.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will accept C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or will read it as an extension.
How much weight the committee gives to attribution clarity and maturity when the only configuration with four supporters, targeted protein degradation, has no approved drug yet.
Whether acknowledging Kosugi and Migita in the background text is enough, or whether the citation wording should signal the antecedent.
Whether Deshaies is indispensable to a degradation citation, and whether Handa's cereblon work should be treated as part of the same achievement or as a separate one.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need is apparent from my profile: I have no personal or institutional connection to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi, and my Masamune and MIT postdoc background is not tied to them. Linke and Sparr are Lund colleagues, which does not bear on any shortlisted candidate. I note that as a synthetic organic chemist I may overweight methodology relative to medical impact.
